title: Remove MainScene.current(): TSP terminal commands get their editor from the terminal that runs them; Scene.instance becomes volatile
description: From the user's review of ENG-25 (2026-10-18). ENG-25 turned MainScene's statics into instance fields and gave code without a passed-in editor MainScene.current(), an unchecked cast of the global Scene.instance (MainScene.java ~307). At the top of the stack 16 files still call it: 13 TSP terminal commands (Add, Move, MoveAfter, MoveBefore, Ask, Color, Comment, Exit, Reset, SubGraph, Update, ...), Knot and Segment hover text, Grid and IrregularQuadGrid coordinate readouts. Problems: (1) the cast is unchecked: a TSP command typed into another scene's terminal (the command registry is global) or hover text built during a switch throws a bare ClassCastException; (2) Scene.instance is written on the render thread during a switch and read by other threads (automation handlers), the same cross-thread case ENG-25 made volatile for IxdarWindow.canvas and AutomationRuntime.canvas, but it is not volatile. Wanted: a terminal belongs to a scene, so commands receive the scene that owns the terminal running them (TSP commands accept only a MainScene host and refuse elsewhere with a terminal message, the way ENG-26's ct refuses tools of another scene type); Knot/Segment/Grid hover and readout text take the editor from their caller; MainScene.current() is deleted; Scene.instance becomes volatile. Repo plan: $REPO_HOME/ai-workspace/reports/repo-plan-2026-10-17.md.
definition-of-done:
1. MainScene.current() no longer exists; no code casts Scene.instance to MainScene.
2. TSP terminal commands run against the scene owning the terminal; typed in a non-TSP scene they print a refusal instead of throwing; a test covers one command in both cases.
3. Scene.instance is volatile.
4. TSP editing behaves as before (load, add, move, ask, colour, reset, subgraph via the terminal; hover text; grid readouts); unit suite and test_cli pass; launch entry and screenshot.
testing-plan:
1. mvn test plus the new command test.
2. Live: ixdar-cli terminal --line commands in ixdar-canvas, and one TSP command in mesh-viewer's terminal.
changes-made: MainScene.current() deleted; nothing casts Scene.instance to MainScene. Terminal holds a final 'scene' (the scene owning it, a constructor argument), replacing the ModelScene-only 'modelScene' field; model/set/collection/ring/explode check it with instanceof as before.

The 13 TSP commands (add, ask, clr, cmt, ex, ma, mb, mv, rst, sg, updt and the static ResetCommand.run(option, editor)) run against terminal.scene and, outside a MainScene, print 'EXCEPTION: <cmd> is a MainScene command' (modelled on ct's '<tool> is a <Host> tool'). ct and ls read terminal.scene instead of Scene.instance.

Knot.toHyperString(editor), Segment.toHyperString(editor, ...), CutMatchList.toHyperString(editor, ...) (no callers) and Grid/IrregularQuadGrid.toCoordString(editor) take the editor from their caller (the knot tools pass their editor field). Scene.instance is volatile.

Test: unit.scenes.MainSceneTerminalCommandTest (ex in the editor's terminal switches to its back scene; ex in a MenuScene terminal prints the refusal and switches nothing). mvn test 530/530, test_cli 96 OK. Live before/after on dsl-51 vs eng-31: ENG-26's tmp/eng-26-tsp.sh output identical; tmp/eng-31-terminal.sh (ask, clr, rst, ls, ct, sg, ld, mv, ma, mb, cmt, updt, add, ex on a scratch copy of djbouti) identical; in mesh-viewer the TSP commands threw ClassCastException on the base and left their text in the command line (next line read 'clrex'); now each prints the refusal (tmp/eng-31-change-mesh-viewer.png).
